intro: If you have overseas income, assets or trusts, or you need to bring previously unreported offshore matters up to date, you may be looking for an offshore tax advisor near you. You want someone who understands the UK rules for foreign income and disclosure, and who can explain your options clearly. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK tax adviser who will quote you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What people searching for an offshore tax advisor near me usually need
need_lead: Offshore tax advisers help with overseas income, trusts and accounts, and with disclosing previously unreported offshore matters.
needs: You receive income from overseas, such as rent, dividends or interest, and need to understand how it is taxed in the UK.
You have a trust or company abroad and are unsure how UK tax rules apply to it.
You have previously unreported offshore income or gains and want to disclose them correctly.
You are moving to the UK or leaving, and need to plan for the tax treatment of your foreign assets.
You have received a letter or enquiry from HMRC about offshore matters and want professional help to respond.
context: HMRC receives information about offshore accounts and income through international agreements, so it is increasingly aware of overseas assets. If you have unreported offshore income, using a disclosure facility can reduce penalties compared with waiting for HMRC to contact you. Trusts abroad have complex UK rules, so specialist advice is often needed.

Tax adviser is not a protected title in the UK. The Chartered Institute of Taxation and the Association of Taxation Technicians are the main specialist bodies, and their members follow Professional Conduct in Relation to Taxation. Tax advisers who charge a fee must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, so it is reasonable to ask about qualifications, supervision and professional indemnity insurance before you go ahead.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Mention that you searched for an offshore tax advisor near me and whether you prefer someone local or are happy to work remotely.
Describe the type of offshore income or assets involved, such as rental property, investments, pensions or a trust.
Say whether the matter is about planning ahead, a current HMRC enquiry, or making a disclosure of previously unreported income.
Give an idea of the countries involved, as different countries have different agreements with the UK.
Explain whether you are an individual, a trustee or a business owner, as this affects the advice needed.
Note any deadlines you are aware of, such as a response date from HMRC, so the adviser can prioritise.
questions: What qualifications and specialist experience do you have in offshore tax matters?
Are you supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes and do you have professional indemnity insurance?
How will you charge for your work, and can you give me an estimate before I commit?
What disclosure facilities might apply to my situation, and what are the likely penalties?
How will you handle information about my overseas assets and keep it confidential?
What information do you need from me to get started, and how long might the process take?

faqs.q: Do I need an offshore tax advisor if I have a small amount of foreign income?
faqs.a: It depends on your circumstances. Even small amounts of foreign income may need to be declared, and a tax adviser can tell you whether you have a reporting obligation. They can also help you avoid mistakes that could lead to penalties.

faqs.q: What is a disclosure facility and how can it help?
faqs.a: A disclosure facility is a way of telling HMRC about previously unreported income or gains. Using one can reduce penalties compared with waiting for HMRC to contact you. An offshore tax adviser can explain which facility suits your situation.

faqs.q: Can I use a local tax adviser for offshore matters?
faqs.a: Yes, many tax advisers handle offshore matters and you can choose someone near you if you prefer face-to-face meetings. However, offshore tax can be complex, so it is worth checking that the adviser has relevant experience. iComply introduces you to a suitable professional based on your needs.

faqs.q: How do I know if a tax adviser is properly qualified?
faqs.a: Tax adviser is not a protected title, so qualifications vary. Look for membership of a recognised body such as the Chartered Institute of Taxation or the Association of Taxation Technicians, and ask about their experience with offshore matters. It is also reasonable to ask about supervision for anti-money-laundering purposes and professional indemnity insurance.
